questions.text: Which body system is responsible for transporting oxygen and nutrients around the body?
questions.markingGuide:
The correct answer is Circulatory system.

Here's why:
The circulatory system (heart, blood, and blood vessels) transports oxygen from the lungs and nutrients from the digestive system to all cells in the body.
The respiratory system brings oxygen into the body but does not transport it to cells.

questions.text: In the hauora model (Te Whare Tapa Whā), which dimension is most closely linked to a person's sense of meaning, identity, and connection to the land?
questions.markingGuide:
The correct answer is Taha wairua (spiritual well-being).

Here's why:
This dimension relates to a person's sense of meaning, purpose, and identity.
It includes connection to the land (whenua), beliefs, values, and feeling that life has purpose.
It is not limited to religion.

questions.text: Explain TWO characteristics of a healthy relationship. For each characteristic, describe how it supports well-being.
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark for each characteristic with a valid link to well-being (2 required).

Possible characteristics: mutual respect — both people value each other's opinions and boundaries, supporting taha hinengaro (feeling valued);.

trust — being able to rely on the other person, which reduces anxiety and supports mental well-being;.

communication — being able to express feelings openly, which prevents misunderstandings and supports emotional health;.

equality — both people have equal say, which supports self-esteem;.

support — encouraging each other's goals, which supports taha wairua (sense of purpose).

questions.text: What is the main health risk associated with vaping for young people in New Zealand?
options: Nicotine addiction and harm to developing brains
It is more dangerous than smoking cigarettes
questions.expectedAnswer: Nicotine addiction and harm to developing brains
questions.markingGuide:
The correct answer is Nicotine addiction and harm to developing brains.

Here's why:
Most vapes contain nicotine, which is highly addictive and particularly harmful to young people whose brains are still developing (until around age 25).
Nicotine can affect memory, concentration, learning, and mood regulation.

questions.text: Describe TWO ways that regular physical activity improves fitness. Link each to a component of fitness (e.g. cardiovascular endurance, muscular strength, flexibility).
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark for each valid way linked to a fitness component (2 required).

For example: Running regularly improves cardiovascular endurance — the heart and lungs become more efficient at delivering oxygen during exercise;.

Weight training improves muscular strength — muscles adapt to increased loads and become stronger;.

Stretching or yoga improves flexibility — joints and muscles increase their range of movement;.

Swimming improves cardiovascular endurance and muscular endurance — the body can sustain effort for longer periods.

questions.text: Which of the following is a protective factor for mental health?
options: Spending excessive time on social media
Having strong connections with whānau and friends
questions.expectedAnswer: Having strong connections with whānau and friends
questions.markingGuide:
The correct answer is Having strong connections with whānau and friends.

Here's why:
Protective factors are things that reduce the risk of developing mental health problems.
Strong social connections provide support, a sense of belonging (taha whānau), and people to talk to during difficult times.

questions.text:
The chart below shows adult obesity rates by ethnicity in New Zealand.

(a) Calculate the difference in obesity rates between the group with the HIGHEST rate and the group with the LOWEST rate.
(b) Explain TWO reasons why obesity is a significant health issue in New Zealand. Include at least one reference to hauora in your answer.
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: (a) Partial credit within the marks below: Highest = Pacific Peoples 64%, Lowest = Asian 16%.

Step 2: Difference = 64 - 16 = 48 percentage points.

Step 3: 1 mark for each valid reason in (b) (2 required), with at least one hauora reference.

Step 4: At least one mark must include the correct calculation in (a).

Step 5: For example: Obesity increases the risk of serious health conditions such as type 2 diabetes, heart disease, and some cancers — this affects taha tinana (physical well-being);.

Step 6: Obesity can lead to low self-esteem, anxiety, and depression, especially in young people who may experience bullying — this affects taha hinengaro (mental/emotional well-being);.

Step 7: NZ has one of the highest rates of childhood obesity in the OECD, putting pressure on the health system;.

Step 8: Obesity is linked to socioeconomic factors — families in lower-income areas may have less access to healthy food and sports facilities, which is a community health issue.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of risk-taking behaviour?
options: Wearing a seatbelt in a car
Going to bed at a regular time
questions.markingGuide:
The correct answer is Texting while driving.

Here's why:
This is a risk-taking behaviour because it significantly increases the chance of a road accident.
Risk-taking behaviours are actions that expose a person (or others) to potential harm.
The other options are all examples of protective or health-promoting behaviours.

questions.text: Describe ONE way a community in New Zealand promotes the health of young people. Explain how this supports at least one dimension of hauora.
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark for identifying a valid community health initiative (e.g. school breakfast programmes like KickStart Breakfast;.

free counselling services through school guidance counsellors;.

sports clubs and community recreation centres;.

Youthline or 1737 helpline;.

Water Safety NZ programmes;.

school health nurses;.

community gardens).

1 mark for explaining how it supports a dimension of hauora (e.g. 'School breakfast programmes support taha tinana by ensuring students have the nutrition they need to learn and be physically well.

It also supports taha whānau by creating a shared, caring environment at school').

questions.text:
A new student has moved to your school from another country. They are finding it hard to make friends and seem withdrawn.

Using the hauora model, explain how this situation could affect their well-being across at least THREE dimensions. Then suggest TWO specific actions the school community could take to support them.
questions.markingGuide:
Up to 2 marks for explaining effects on at least 3 dimensions of hauora: Taha whānau (social) — they are separated from their friends and family networks, and struggling to build new connections at school, leading to loneliness;.

Taha hinengaro (mental/emotional) — feeling isolated may cause anxiety, sadness, or low self-esteem;.

Taha wairua (spiritual) — they may feel a loss of identity and purpose, disconnected from their culture and the things that gave their life meaning;.

Taha tinana (physical) — stress and loneliness can affect sleep, appetite, and physical health.

Must address 3 dimensions well for 1 mark, all 4 with depth for 2 marks.

1 mark for suggesting TWO practical actions (e.g. a buddy system where an existing student is paired with the new student;.

a school cultural diversity day where the new student can share their culture;.

teachers checking in regularly;.

inviting them to join a sports team or club;.

having a peer support group;.

ensuring the school has a welcoming environment that values different cultures).
